Command: A Nazirite shall not defile himself for the dead
Summary: Throughout the vow, the Nazirite comes at no dead body, not even for father, mother, brother, or sister, lest his consecration be defiled.
Commandment: A Nazirite shall not come at any dead body for all the days of his separation.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Acts 21:23-26 shows Paul joining men under a vow in Jerusalem, which shows the practice continued among Jewish believers, not that it is imposed on Christians.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the Nazirite separates himself unto the LORD (Numbers 6:2,5-6); no further reason is given, so the components' purposes are traditional — corpse-avoidance as the priest-like holiness of the vow.
